div.div: The Problem: If you run kubectl delete pod --force --grace-period=0, you are telling Linux to kill the process immediately without letting it close files or flush its cache. If the DB was mid-write, the filesystem metadata can become garbled.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 528px; height: 1px; padding-top: 230px; margin-left: 281px;

div.div: The Fix: Never force-delete a database pod unless the node is already physically gone. If corruption happens, you must restore from your last known good snapshot and let the database "replay" its Write-Ahead Log (WAL) to catch up to the last valid transaction.
